critique.good: The status columns are compact and easy to compare, while the generous Notes column keeps the advisory URL intact and gives prose a comfortable measure. The long package wraps at break points, and its row still reads as a unit.
critique.problems: The prerelease version breaks across two lines, and the long package occupies three lines.
critique.cause: Version is only 90px wide, leaving 69px for text; Package is 187px wide, leaving little room beyond its longest unbreakable segment.

critique.good: The wide Package column reduces the long identifier to two lines. License and vulnerability values remain easy to scan.
critique.problems: Notes become narrow and tall across several rows, and the advisory URL splits within a word. The prerelease version also wraps.
critique.cause: Package takes 300px, leaving Notes only 223px and Version 82px.

critique.good: Package, License and Vulnerabilities have clear headers, and the status values remain easy to compare.
critique.problems: The long package and prerelease version still wrap, while the advisory URL splits within a word. Several rows are tall despite the extra space given to Package and Vulnerabilities.
critique.cause: Notes at 260px is too narrow for its 280px unbreakable segment; Version at 100px is too narrow for its longest one-line value. Vulnerabilities uses 160px even though its header fits at 135px.

critique.good: The version strings and audit columns are easy to scan, and all headers fit on one line. The long package identifier wraps across three lines while remaining visually tied to its row.
critique.problems: The advisory URL splits within its long token, making it harder to follow. The notes and package columns both create three-line cells, but in different rows.
critique.cause: Notes is 296px wide, leaving 275px for text—5px less than its longest unbreakable content.

critique.good: The wider Notes column avoids the reported mid-word split. License and vulnerability values remain compact and align well for vertical comparison.
critique.problems: The pre-release version wraps onto a second line, interrupting the package–version identification pair. The long package identifier still needs three lines.
critique.cause: Version is reduced to 110px, leaving 89px for text, while Notes receives 308px.

critique.good: The full pre-release version stays on one line, the headers remain intact, and the status columns are easy to compare.
critique.problems: The long package identifier breaks at a less natural point, separating a hyphen from the preceding segment. That makes the identifier harder to read even though the table height is unchanged.
critique.cause: Package is 182px wide, leaving 161px for text—5px less than its longest unbreakable segment. Notes has the 301px needed for its longest segment.

critique.good: All headers and license names stay intact. The package, audit-status columns, and notes remain easy to scan, and the long package identifier wraps at natural break points.
critique.problems: The prerelease version wraps onto two lines, making the version harder to read as a single identifier. The advisory note also occupies three lines, though its URL remains readable at break points.
critique.cause: The 117px Version column provides 96px of text space, less than the 101px needed for the longest version. The 301px Notes column has limited room for the long advisory URL.

critique.good: The wider Version column keeps the prerelease version on one line. Headers remain intact and the overall row rhythm is unchanged.
critique.problems: The Proprietary license splits within the word, disrupting the vertical scan of license values and making that cell look cramped.
critique.cause: Reducing License to 101px leaves 80px of text space, 5px short of the longest license name.

understanding.purpose: Audit English-language dependencies, their versions, licenses, vulnerabilities, and associated notes.
understanding.reading: Readers scan package names to find dependencies, then read across each row to assess license and vulnerability status alongside the notes. Vulnerability counts and license values also invite vertical comparison.
groups: Package and Version identify the installed dependency.
License and Vulnerabilities summarize audit status and should be easy to compare down the table.
Notes provide context for the audit findings and belong visually with their row.
keep_intact: Long unbreakable text in Notes where space permits
may_wrap: Notes prose can wrap at word boundaries.
Long package text can wrap at available break points; wrapped notes in the same row can absorb some of that height.

bad.why: The narrow Notes column breaks the advisory URL mid-word and makes several rows unnecessarily tall, while Vulnerabilities has surplus space.
The License column splits “Proprietary” into “Proprietar” and an isolated “y,” making a short categorical value harder to scan.

final.rationale: r2A keeps all headers and license values intact while giving Notes enough room to wrap the advisory URL at a natural break. The long package name and prerelease version wrap at hyphens, and the rows remain easy to scan across. Compared with r1B, its slightly wider Version column gives that identifier more breathing room without worsening the visible Notes wrapping.

general: Protect short headers and categorical values from mid-word breaks, especially when they must be scanned down a column.
Allocate width according to content and reading task; prose and identifiers often need more room than short status values.
Judge wrapping by where breaks occur and how the whole row reads, not by table height alone.
specific: The advisory URL benefits from roughly 301 px or more in Notes, while License needs 106 px to keep “Proprietary” intact.
The long package name can wrap at hyphens, but reducing Package below 187 px causes an internal word break in the shown candidates.

final.tradeoffs: r1B gives more space to Notes, while r1A and r3A keep the prerelease version on one line at the cost of a mid-word URL break. A designer might value the intact version more highly than the URL break.
final.uncertain: The ranges are conservative visual estimates, not browser-tested boundaries; each varies one column while the others retain approximately their preferred proportions within the 846 px limit. The rendered candidates do not establish every breakpoint.

A.why: Equal column widths waste space in short-value columns and squeeze Notes into many short lines; the long package name also breaks awkwardly inside a word.

B.why: Notes has useful space and the rows scan cleanly, but the long package name and prerelease version wrap, making those identifiers harder to follow.

C.why: The wider package column gives its long name a somewhat more natural wrap, while Notes remains readable; the prerelease version still breaks across lines.

D.why: The columns are well balanced and the notes read comfortably, though the long package name and prerelease version wrap.

E.why: The package column handles the long name reasonably, but Notes is cramped: prose takes extra lines and the advisory identifier breaks within its prefix. The version also wraps.

F.why: The prerelease version stays on one line and Notes is readable; the long package name still spans three lines, and the advisory URL wraps.

reviews.unsure: The trade-off between preserving the version on one line and giving the package name or Notes slightly more space is close; the advisory URL wraps in every layout.

A.why: The notes have comfortable space and the rows scan clearly, but the long package name and prerelease version both wrap.

B.why: Equal column widths leave notes cramped and create tall rows, while the long package name breaks within a word.

C.why: The prerelease version stays intact, notes read comfortably, and the long package name wraps at hyphens. The advisory URL still breaks across lines.

D.why: Notes have room and the package name wraps at hyphens, but the narrow version column splits the prerelease identifier.

E.why: The notes are readable and the rows are compact, but both the long package name and prerelease version wrap.

F.why: The wider package column preserves useful hyphen breaks, but the narrower notes column creates taller rows and breaks the advisory identifier; the prerelease version also wraps.

reviews.unsure: The long package name and advisory URL must wrap under this width constraint; the preferred tradeoff depends partly on how often readers need to copy those identifiers.
